title: instant karma?
hookLine: the vending machine tips over, everyone says karma: what the Buddha actually meant
carry: I am the owner of my actions

cards: Instant karma. A man kicks a vending machine and it tips over onto him. Someone cuts the line and their coffee comes out wrong.
Everyone in the comments reaches for the same word, and they mean payback: the universe as a referee, settling scores where you can watch. It's satisfying.
It's also not what the Buddha meant, and his version points the other way: back at the one acting. First, a guess.

teach.b: Karma, or kamma in Pali, means action. A deed. Something done.
In one discourse he says it plainly: intention is what I call karma. Before the hand moves or the words come out, there's a leaning, a choice. That's where it starts.
The old texts use a farming picture: deeds are seeds, and their results ripen like fruit. Not because a judge is keeping score. Because that's what seeds do.
Two surprises. First, it's mostly about the one acting. Every choice shapes the chooser: patience, practiced, makes a patient person.
Second, not everything is karma. Asked whether everything a person feels comes from past deeds, the Buddha said no: illness, weather, accidents and other people's choices play their part.
So 'they deserved it' was never the point.

teach.h: I AM THE OWNER OF MY ACTIONS.
teach.b: In many temples and monasteries, people chant a reflection on it: I am the owner of my actions, heir to my actions.

how: Buddhists understand karma as intentional action and what it ripens into; in many temples and monasteries a daily reflection is chanted that ends 'I am the owner of my actions, heir to my actions', and people try to act from kind intentions in ordinary life.

games.q: a man asks the Buddha: is everything a person feels caused by their own past deeds? what does the Buddha answer?
o: no: illness, weather and accidents play a part too.
games.why: he says no, and lists other causes, from illness to the seasons to accidents. karma is real, but it isn't everything.

games.q: put the old line back together.

practice: One breath with the bell. Bring to mind the next thing you'll do: a message, a meeting, a meal. Breathe in, and notice the intention underneath it.
Breathe out, and let it lean toward kindness, if you like. That leaning is where karma starts.

wordCard.voice: Karma. Action, and the intention inside it: what you mean, and what it grows. First word on your strand.

carryVoice: Your line: I am the owner of my actions. Not a weight to carry. A handle you can hold. See you tomorrow.

sources.ref: Nibbedhika Sutta (Anguttara Nikaya 6.63): intention is kamma
